chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb and Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about the leftover water of riding animals, sheep, and cattle: may wudu (ablution) be performed with it and may it be drunk? He said: “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.سُؤْرِ: leftover water or remains from which an animal has drunk
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform wudu (ablution) and drink from water left over by animals?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that the leftover water from animals such as riding animals, sheep, and cattle is permissible for both drinking and wudu (ablution). It indicates the taharah (ritual purity) of such water and its usability in acts of worship.
